Problem_Classification.Domain: Deep Learning / Computer Vision — CNN inference primitive
Problem_Classification.Algorithm: 2D Max Pooling applied over a batch of feature maps (kernel name is "maxpool3d" but the third dimension is batch/channel, not a true spatial Z; window is purely 2D)
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: Down-samples each 2D image/feature-map by taking the maximum value within each non-overlapping pool_width × pool_height window (2×2 here, since pool size == stride). Output spatial dims = input/2 in both axes; batch dim preserved.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. Host: allocate H×W×N float buffer, fill with rand()%256/255. 2. cudaMalloc d_image and d_result; H2D copy of input. 3. Launch maxpool3d with grid = (ceil(Wo/8), ceil(Ho/8), ceil(N/4)) and block = (8,8,4) = 256 threads. 4. Each thread maps to one (x,y,z) output element. It computes input base index (xidx=2x, yidx=2y) and loops r∈[0,2), c∈[0,2): reads 4 input elements with fmaxf, init max=0. 5. Writes single max to o_img[((z*Ho)+y)*Wo + x]. 6. Repeat 'repeat' times; D2H copy; CPU re-computes ground truth and memcmp-verifies.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(N · Wo · Ho · pool_w · pool_h) = O(N·W·H) since pool=stride=2 ⇒ each input element visited exactly once. Space: O(N·W·H) input + O(N·W·H/4) output ≈ 1.25·N·W·H·sizeof(float).

Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Per output element: 4 input loads + 1 output store = 5 × 4 B = 20 B traffic (assuming no L1/L2 reuse beyond what hardware coalesces; with perfect coalescing the input bytes are still 16 B and output 4 B = 20 B). Useful work per output: 3 fmaxf ops (≈3 "FLOPs"), plus ~4 integer index ops which aren't FLOPs. AI ≈ 3 FLOP / 20 B = 0.15 FLOP/B. Even counting the init compare with 0, AI ≤ 0.20 FLOP/B.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: RTX A6000 peak FP32 ≈ 38.7 TFLOPS, peak BW ≈ 768 GB/s ⇒ ridge ≈ 38700/768 ≈ 50 FLOP/B. Kernel AI (0.15) is ~330× below the ridge ⇒ deeply in the memory-bound regime.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: Global memory bandwidth (DRAM throughput). Secondary limiter: uncoalesced / strided load pattern that wastes effective bandwidth and possibly L1 sector efficiency. Compute units are largely idle.

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Sliding-window with stride == window (i.e. non-overlapping tiles). Globally a streaming read of the full input with strided gather per warp due to the (x,y) row interleave.
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: 4:1 (4 input loads per 1 store per output)
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: 1.0 — because pool_w == Hstride and pool_h == Vstride, every input element is read exactly once across the whole kernel. No algorithmic reuse; shared memory would only help by improving coalescing, not by reducing traffic.
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Requires transformation. With blockDim=(8,8,4), a warp of 32 threads contains threadIdx.x∈[0,7] × threadIdx.y∈[0,3] (z fixed). Within a warp, threads with the same y but different x access input addresses (z·H+2y+r)·W + 2x for c=0 — i.e., stride-2 along the row. For each r,c iteration the warp issues stride-2 accesses spanning 8 consecutive (x*2) positions plus 4 rows ⇒ multiple 32-byte sectors per memory transaction, effective bandwidth utilization ≈ 50%. A 1D layout (e.g. blockDim.x = 32 or 64, contiguous along output-x) plus an outer loop over r would coalesce perfectly.
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: Two viable strategies: (a) Coalesce-only fix: blockDim = (32, 4, 1) or (64, 2, 1), one thread per output pixel; rely on L1/L2 for the second row. No shared memory needed (≈0 B/block). (b) Shared-memory tile: load a (2·BX) × (2·BY) input tile per block into SMEM, then 2×2 reduce. For BX=BY=16 → 32×32 input tile = 4096 B per block (well within 100 KB SM budget), enabling fully coalesced 128-byte loads and trivial intra-warp reduction. Either choice should approach DRAM peak; strategy (a) is simpler and likely sufficient since reuse factor is 1.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: One thread per output element (x,y,z). Each thread does 4 loads + 3 max + 1 store.
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Fully independent — no cross-thread data dependency, no reduction across blocks.
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: None in the current kernel. Would need __syncthreads() only if a shared-memory tiling variant is introduced.
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: Current (8,8,4)=256 threads is acceptable but x-dimension is too narrow for coalescing. Theoretical recommendation for CC 8.6 (1536 threads/SM, 16 blocks/SM max): • 256 threads/block as (32,8,1) — 6 blocks/SM, 100% occupancy ceiling on threads, 1 warp per row → perfect coalescing. • Or 128 threads (32,4,1) — 12 blocks/SM, also full thread occupancy and lower per-block resource pressure. Register usage of this kernel is small (~16–20 regs), so occupancy will not be register-limited.

Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_Block: 99 KB (101376 B) opt-in maximum; 48 KB default static limit
Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_SM: 100 KB (102400 B) unified L1/SMEM partition; up to 100 KB usable as SMEM
Hardware_Constraints.Peak_Memory_Bandwidth: ≈768 GB/s (8001 MHz GDDR6 × 384 b / 8 = 768.1 GB/s theoretical; ECC-on slightly less in practice)
Hardware_Constraints.GPU_Clock_Rate: 2100 MHz max SM clock (from nvidia-smi); base ~1410 MHz

Data_Shape.Input_Dimensions: Runtime-parameterized: input N × H × W, output N × (H/2) × (W/2), pool = stride = 2×2. N, H, W supplied as argv[3], argv[2], argv[1].
Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Device: d_image = 4·N·W·H B + d_result = 4·N·(W/2)·(H/2) B = 1.25 · 4 · N·W·H B. Host: h_image + h_output + d_output mirror = 4·N·W·H + 2·4·N·(W/2)·(H/2) = 1.5 · 4 · N·W·H B. Example (N=512, W=H=1024): device ≈ 2.5 GB, host ≈ 3.0 GB; fits within the 49 GB VRAM and 188 GB RAM available.
